In Saints Row: The Third, players can engage in various activities, some of which were introduced in previous Saints Row games. These diversions serve the plot, either by training the player-character or damaging the Syndicate, and can be repeated. Outside of structured diversions, there are also occasional poems signed "M.M.", though the source texts have been lost. "To William Drummond of Hawthornden" is one such dedicatory poem, which opens with formulaic humility: "I Never rested on the Muses bed, Nor dipt my trembling hand in Phoebus's spring."

In one episode of the reality TV show "Hollywood Game Night," contestants participated in a game called "Movie Sound Effects Challenge." In this game, teams were given props and had to add sound effects in sync to five silent video clips from previous seasons. By successfully completing this challenge, teams received their next clue. Teams were then instructed to find the home of the LA Galaxy: the StubHub Center.

This transition came about following a significant event in the life of the show's producer, Sean Hayes: the unexpected passing of his mother, who was the sole supporter of his filmmaking aspirations. As Hayes has said, "It was a significant blow when my mother, who was the only one in my family to support my passion for filmmaking, passed away. At that time, I realized that I needed to take a step back and reassess my priorities."
